text: A Personal Developer Instance, or PDI, is a free, full-featured ServiceNow instance that anyone can request through ServiceNow's developer program at developer dot servicenow dot com. It's a genuine, complete instance — not a stripped-down demo, not a simulator, not some sandboxed subset of the platform. Underneath, it's the exact same Now Platform a paying customer runs, on the same release family ServiceNow is currently shipping.

Requesting a PDI through the developer portal makes you the admin on it — full administrative access, not a limited guest role. You can create tables, build forms, write Business Rules and Client Scripts, configure Access Control Lists, and install additional applications from the ServiceNow Store, exactly the way a real customer's admin could in their own Development instance.

ServiceNow also loads every PDI with sample and demo data — demo users, demo incidents, demo Configuration Items in the CMDB, and sample records across most of the major applications. That's genuinely useful for learning: you can explore Incident Management, reporting, and the CMDB with realistic-looking data the moment the instance finishes provisioning, instead of starting from a completely empty database.

A PDI does come with real limitations worth knowing up front. It's a learning and building tool, not a production system. A PDI left unused for a period of inactivity — commonly around two weeks, though that threshold has shifted over time — goes dormant to save resources, and has to be explicitly woken up from the developer portal before you can log back in. It isn't deleted, just paused. PDIs are also licensed strictly for learning, prototyping, and personal skill-building, never for running a real business's actual IT service management, and they run on lighter shared infrastructure than a paid customer instance.

None of that makes a PDI any less real as a learning environment. It's the same platform, the same applications, the same admin capability — it simply isn't meant to stay awake forever or carry a real business's workload.

This course's labs are written as worked scenarios, with real table names, field names, and menu paths, detailed enough to follow conceptually with no instance open at all, or to replicate step by step on your own PDI if you have one requested and awake.
